scope: Source-linked protected32 multi-block trace design and standalone nonterminal branch side-exit proof; no production dispatcher/WASM integration or full workload measurement

proof.compiler: Ubuntu clang 18.1.3 (1ubuntu1), wasm32 -O3; exact flags in proof script
proof.wasmArtifactLocation: Temporary directory only; no binary is committed
proof.cases: 6/6 ordinary I80386 parity: taken nonterminal JNZ side exit before fallthrough; not-taken continuation through two successor NOPs; event budgets of 1, 2, 3 and 4 instructions with exact EIP, registers, flags and CPU cycles
proof.limit: The event budget is supplied to the standalone WASM loop; this proof does not compute real AT chip/LAPIC deadlines or validate multi-page code windows. Those remain integration gates.

opportunity.notYetMeasured: Disjoint linkable-successor call count and post-packed V8 entry share on the current source. The design predeclares gates before either full xv6 measurement.
opportunity.preCodeGate: A disjoint current-source successor census must find at least 1.5 million call boundaries elidable in two-or-more-block first-tranche traces. Exclude branches already linked in one native call, chip/LAPIC deadline exits, invalidated blocks, self-loop/budget artifacts and cold/missing/unsafe successors. Separately, a post-packed V8 profile must put at least 15% of self samples in the affected entry path. Both are necessary, not sufficient.
opportunity.retentionGate: After focused differential tests and full guest/RAM parity, at least 5% lower mean user CPU in three serial paired xv6 A/B runs with all pairs favorable. Measure Windows separately.

safety: First tranche uses only already supported register-only forms, prevalidates all constituent code windows/bytes once at trace entry, excludes every write and control-state change, clips per-instruction execution to existing event horizons, and side-exits at the exact next EIP. A later dynamic read tranche must use only already-valid mirrored translations and slow-exit before faultable/MMIO/page-crossing accesses; JS owns page walks, A/D bits, CR2 and faults. No speed claim is made.
